## Observation
The `sweep (windows)` job 135597358757 (run 44534782876, main at fa383b1d195, 2026-11-19) failed `tests/unit/test_fixture_env_repr_security.py::test_fixture_failure_does_not_render_unrelated_ambient_secret[tests.scripts.test_observability_exit-healthy_env-None]` at line 71 (`assert result.returncode == 1`). The child pytest session ended with `ERROR collecting test session`: `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]` from `Path.lstat()` on `C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\rebar-ticket-view-534ea34f-s5jdm9m4`. That is a directory in the shared system temp dir, apparently created and then removed by another xdist worker's pinned-ticket-view while the child was enumerating temp. The same test passed in the sweep of run 44526811291 (job 135569438854, main at f8e9ea0e61f) one hour earlier. It is not in any deselect argfile. It recurred in run 44560626779 (job 135688612206, main at 91322a91e9e) on `test_short_traceback_is_a_non_rendering_control[...signals_gerrit_config...]`.

## Root cause (confirmed)
Version: the Windows sweep installs pytest 9.2.0 (`pytest==9.2.0` in job 135688612206's install log; `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `uv pip install`, unpinned within `pytest>=8,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1` in `pyproject.toml:250`). The 3 code paths below were read in the pytest 9.2.0 source (`src/_pytest/config/findpaths.py`, `src/_pytest/main.py`, `src/_pytest/pathlib.py` at tag 9.2.0) and are identical in the locally locked 9.0.3 (`.venv/.../_pytest/config/findpaths.py:313-330`, `_pytest/main.py:911-916` and `:977-982`, `_pytest/pathlib.py:1007-1016` and `:1058-1063`).
The child runs with cwd = the repo (`D:\a\rebar\rebar`), while its test file lives under pytest's tmp_path on `C:` (`%TEMP%\pytest-of-runneradmin\...`). The Windows sweep is the only CI job that passes no `--basetemp` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:296-299`).
1. `determine_setup` (findpaths): with no ini file, rootdir = `get_common_ancestor(invocation_dir, [invocation_dir, ancestor])`, and only if that is a filesystem root (`is_fs_root`) does it fall back to the arguments' own directory. `commonpath` (`_pytest/pathlib.py`) catches the `ValueError` that `ntpath.commonpath` raises for 2 drives ("Paths don't have the same drive") and returns `None`, so the common ancestor stays the cwd. Rootdir and confcutdir become the repo.
2. `Session.collect` (main.py): every ancestor of the argument that `_is_in_confcutdir` accepts joins the collection path. No `C:` path is under a `D:` confcutdir, so collection starts at `C:\` and runs `Dir.collect` (scandir) on `C:\Users\...\Temp`.
3. Same function: on `sys.platform == "win32"`, each scanned entry that does not equal the next path part goes through `samefile_nofollow(node.path, matchparts[0])`, which calls `p1.lstat()`. A `rebar-ticket-view-*` sibling removed by another worker between the scandir and the lstat raises `FileNotFoundError`. That is the frame that enumerates `%TEMP%`.
Reproduced on macOS (probe in session scratch): with the child's cwd and test file sharing a non-root ancestor, `_pytest.main` seeing `win32`, and a sibling removed after its parent's scan, the child gives `ERROR collecting test session` / `FileNotFoundError` and rc 2. Each control that drops 1 of the 3 conditions passes.

## Approach
Fix the class in the single sanctioned launcher, `tests/_nested_pytest.py::run_nested_pytest`, which every nested child uses (enforced by `tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py`). A new pure function `_rootdir_pin(args, cwd, *, pathmod=os.path, exists=os.path.exists, isdir=os.path.isdir)` returns `["--rootdir", <dir>]` or `[]`, and the helper appends it to the child's arguments. It applies pytest's own `get_dirs_from_args` rule, so it sees exactly the paths pytest would: each argument not starting with `-`, cut at `::`, that exists on disk. A directory stands for itself and a file for its parent. pytest makes the same choice for option values (such as the value after `-k`), and such a value only counts if it is an existing absolute path. Then:
- it returns `[]` if the caller passed `--rootdir`, `-c`/`--config-file` or `--confcutdir`, in the bare, `=`-joined or attached (`-cFILE`) spelling;
- it returns `[]` if no argument is an absolute existing path, or if any one lies under the cwd (case-folded with `pathmod.normcase`). Repo-relative and in-repo callers therefore keep pytest's rootdir, ini file and conftest loading unchanged;
- otherwise it returns `--rootdir` = `pathmod.commonpath` of those directories, or `[]` when they are on different drives (`ValueError` caught).
This pins what a macOS run already gets: rootdir and confcutdir become the test file's directory, so collection never lists the shared system temp. The `pathmod`/`exists`/`isdir` parameters follow `_child_env`'s `os_name` injection, so the Windows layout is testable on any OS. No config key, env var or flag. Out of scope: launches that bypass the helper (pytester, and console-script runs whose cwd is their own tmp_path), because they do not hit this layout.

## Behaviour change on POSIX (measured)
On POSIX the pin changes rootdir only when the cwd and the test file share a non-root ancestor. Linux CI is such a case: its `--basetemp` under `${{ runner.temp }}` shares `/home/runner/work` with the checkout, so a child there is rooted at `/home/runner/work` today. Measured on macOS with the same layout (basetemp under `/Users/joeoakhart/scratch`, sharing `/Users/joeoakhart` with the checkout): the 19 modules that call `run_nested_pytest` gave 223 passed, 2 skipped both before and after the change. Under the checkout's own basetemp, also 223 passed, 2 skipped.

## Scope
- `tests/_nested_pytest.py`: `_rootdir_pin`, helpers for option detection and containment, and the call in `run_nested_pytest`.
- `tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py`: regression tests.

## Testing
- Pure function with `ntpath` and injected `exists`/`isdir`: cwd `D:\a\rebar\rebar` with a `C:\...\Temp\...\test_render_fixture.py` argument (and its `::node` form) gives `--rootdir` = that file's directory. A directory argument gives itself. Each of these gives `[]`: a relative argument, an absolute argument under cwd (also in other letter case), no path argument, a caller `--rootdir`/`--rootdir=`/`-c`/`-cFILE`/`--config-file=`/`--confcutdir`, a non-existent absolute argument, and arguments on 2 drives. An option value that is not a path (`-k expr`) is ignored.
- End to end on any OS: the child's cwd and test file share a non-root ancestor that holds a `conftest.py` raising at import. Before the fix the child loads it and fails; after the fix it passes, which proves collection no longer walks above the test file's directory.
- Existing helper tests stay green (`test_the_call_contract_reaches_subprocess_run` passes no path argument, so its exact command is unchanged). `make verify`.

## Portability
Pure `os.path`/`ntpath` string logic plus `os.path.exists`/`isdir`: no fds, no signals, no `/tmp`, and the cross-drive `ValueError` is caught.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified with the frame that enumerates the temp dir.
- [ ] The enumeration tolerates entries removed concurrently, or the child no longer shares the system temp dir, with a regression test that does not need Windows.
- [ ] The test passes in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix (run id recorded in a comment).
